text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Communications Minister Jassem al-Oun says new mobile telephones firm to be opened for subscription in two months. The move is aimed at ending a monoploy by Mobile Telephone Company (MTC) to facilitate the privatisation of the sector.
- Length of military conscription might be reduced but not abolished, Defence Ministry source says.
- Kuwait's Investment Projects Company sold 80 million of its Al-Ahli Bank shares to Securities Group.
- Only seven MPs and one minister showed up for parliament's Saturday session. The 62-man parliament will meet on Tuesday.
- Government requests the discussion of security issues at parliament.
- Kuwait to take part in an international conference in China on May 13 on desertification.
- University professors threaten to go on strike if salaries are not raised by the end of May.
- Kuwait's Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah sends condolences to Iran's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani after Saturday's earthquake.
- United Nations Crime-Prevention and Criminal Justice Committee praised child-protection laws in Kuwait in its meetings which concluded in Vienna on Friday.

- MP proposes bill to allow police and army members to vote in national elections. Like women, Kuwaitis under 21 and those naturalised less than 20 years, military and police personnel do not have the right to vote.
